title: wire.h: compile-time assert block placed outside header guards scope could fire in unexpected TUs
description: The wc_static_assert2() calls in crypto2dev_wire.h are inside the #ifndef WOLFSSL_PORT_CRYPTO2DEV_WIRE_H guard, so they fire only once per TU on first include. Correct. However, the assertions appear after the ioctl code block, outside the #ifndef CRYPTO2DEV_IOC_INIT guard. This means if CRYPTO2DEV_HAVE_UAPI_HEADER is defined (the alternate path mentioned in the header comment), the structs from the uapi header are used but the wc_static_assert2() calls still fire against those struct sizes. The comment says 'These values must match the kernel driver's uapi header' — correct, but the structs being asserted against may be from the uapi header, not wire.h, leading to either passing (good) or failing (catches actual mismatch). The intent is correct but the comment about 'replicate minimum subset' combined with the assert is confusing: the assert fires regardless of which header defined the structs.
